biggest_gap: Side A loses most often (7 of 13 decided steps). Whenever the wanted text was an older clip, not the latest, the person had to run a manual clipboard-history lookup. They pressed ⌘V and then trimmed four times, or opened Spotlight, pressed ⌘4, typed a search word, pressed Return and then ⌘V. That cost 2.75 s to 4.19 s of hands-on effort, against 2.0 s to 2.25 s for a single numbered pick on side B. Side A has no one-key route to an older clip.
notes: 32 of 45 steps are identical plain ⌘V landings at 0.28 s, so nothing separates the sides there. Side A got no wrong text in any step, and neither did B. Side B's winning route (hotkey + digit) is not free. The app made the person wait 250-360 ms before the list appeared on steps 7, 8, 38, 39, 43, 44 and 45, which is noticeable and always above the ~300 ms line on steps 39, 43, 44 and 45. The person must also read a list and pick a number. Steps 17, 25, 44 and 45 needed typed letters in the list on top of that, so the wins there are about 1 s, not 2 s. Step 5 on side B shows a 2.0 s route with only an 86 ms wait, the best case for the hotkey. A's ⌘V-then-trim×4 route (steps 5, 7, 8, 14, 26, 38) is slower than the pure hotkey route by about 0.55 s every time, and it is ugly because a wrong paste lands first and is then trimmed. Steps 10, 21 and 42 (plain-wanted and secure fields) came out the same on both sides, and step 35 landed the same acceptable commit URL on both.
